display.title: Before Modeh Ani: Remember That Hashem Is Right Beside You
display.summary_short: What do we do even before saying Modeh Ani? The Shulchan Aruch begins by reminding us that Hashem is right at our bedside.
display.summary_long: A short mitzvah-time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi asks what is the very first thing we do when we wake up. Most children would answer 'Modeh Ani', but there is something even before that. In the Shulchan Aruch, the law of saying Modeh Ani comes in the second paragraph of the first chapter. The very first paragraph teaches 'Shivisi Hashem l'negdi samid': we set Hashem before us at all times. Modeh Ani thanks Hashem for returning our neshamah, but first we remind ourselves that Hashem was right at our bedside all night long, watching over and protecting us, and it is to Him that we then say Modeh Ani.
display.lesson: When you wake up, first remember that Hashem is right beside you, then thank Him with Modeh Ani.
